audit.whatIsWrong: The entry invents an ability called the "passive Force Pulse shield" and builds three lines on it: spikes[0] "before his passive shield regenerates", wants.you[1] "Keep him perpetually below 50% HP so his passive Force Pulse shield cannot absorb enough", whys[0] "Kassadin's passive Force Pulse shield is magic-damage only and irrelevant at level 1".
audit.why: This fuses three separate abilities into one thing that does not exist, and it gets the matchup exactly backwards. Kassadin's PASSIVE is Void Stone — he takes REDUCED MAGIC DAMAGE and ignores unit collision. The magic-absorbing SHIELD is on Null Sphere (Q). Force Pulse is his E, a charged cone slow. There is also no 50% HP threshold anywhere in his kit. The consequence is severe: the entry declares his passive 'irrelevant at level 1' when Void Stone is in fact permanently relevant to Tahm Kench specifically, because Devour deals MAGIC damage. Kassadin's passive is a standing discount on Tahm Kench's ultimate, and the entry tells the player to ignore it.
audit.corrected: Void Stone (P) = permanent magic damage reduction, which blunts Devour. The shield is on Null Sphere. Force Pulse is the E cone slow. No HP threshold exists.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json — P Void Stone: 'takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision'; Q Null Sphere: 'granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage'; E Force Pulse: 'damage and slow enemies in a cone'. champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour: 'dealing magic damage if they are an enemy'

audit.whatIsWrong: Null Sphere is called a silence four times — early "his only tool is Null Sphere's slow-projectile silence... so the silence lands after your first stack", mid "which silences you briefly and stops a Devour cast" and "so a Null Sphere silence cannot interrupt the Devour", wants.foe[0] "Use Null Sphere's silence to interrupt your Devour cast".
audit.why: Null Sphere interrupts CHANNELS. It is not a silence in the live kit — Riot's own text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels', and the kit's derived flag vocabulary includes a 'silence' flag that Null Sphere does not carry (its flags are projectile, shield, channel). The distinction decides the matchup's central question. Neither Tongue Lash nor Devour is a channel, so Null Sphere cannot stop either of them — whereas a silence would stop both. The entry therefore invents a threat that dictates its entire trading pattern ('only commit the stun when you have the third stack confirmed so a Null Sphere silence cannot interrupt the Devour'), and the caution it recommends is unnecessary.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere interrupts channels, not casts. It cannot stop Tongue Lash or Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json — Q Null Sphere description: 'dealing damage and interrupting channels'; flags are projectile+shield+channel with no silence flag, although the kit's flag set does include silence as a derivable flag
champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — neither Q nor R carries a channel flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk is said to wipe An Acquired Taste stacks in three places: spikes[2] "blink through your Tongue Lash arc and reset the stack count", wants.foe[1] "Kite with Riftwalk blinks at level 6 to reset your An Acquired Taste stacks", whys[4] "genuinely resetting your stacks".
audit.why: Nothing in Kassadin's kit removes An Acquired Taste stacks and nothing in Tahm Kench's kit loses them to a blink. Stacks are consumed when the Q stun fires; that is the only consumption clause Riot states. This is the same invented mechanic I found in the Heimerdinger entry, where the grenade was said to 'reset your stack count to zero'. It changes behaviour for the worse — a player who believes his stacks are wiped every time Kassadin blinks will stop holding partial stacks through a Riftwalk, which is precisely when he should be holding them.
audit.corrected: Blinking does not touch the stacks. Riftwalk moves him out of range; the banked stacks stay banked.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q: 'If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed' (sole consumption clause); champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json — R has no stack-removal clause

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] claims "Three An Acquired Taste stacks turn Devour into a silence-immune lockdown — his Null Sphere cannot interrupt it once stacks are confirmed".
audit.why: Three stacks confers no immunity of any kind — it is purely the gate that makes Devour castable on an enemy champion. Nothing about reaching three stacks makes a subsequent cast uninterruptible. This also directly contradicts wants.foe[0] in the same entry, which says Kassadin should use Null Sphere to interrupt the Devour cast; the file argues both sides of an interaction that, per the point above, does not exist in either direction.
audit.corrected: Three stacks is a cast requirement, not a protection.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — P An Acquired Taste: 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup as having zero cooldown-sequencing advice, and that is accurate — there is not one concrete number in the entry, and the only sequencing line, "Force him to Riftwalk in before you throw Q rather than after", has no timing attached to it.
audit.why: The numbers here are unusually decisive. Tongue Lash reaches 900 and Null Sphere only 650, so Tahm Kench has a clean 250-unit bully range pre-6 that the entry gestures at but never quantifies. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2 seconds — so short that 'reads on his blink cooldown' is not a real plan; what actually limits him is the escalating mana cost of repeated casts, not the cooldown. Force Pulse is 21/20/19/18/17, by far his longest laning cooldown and the genuine punish window. Null Sphere is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7.
audit.corrected: Give the 900-vs-650 range gap pre-6, and point the punish at Force Pulse's ~21s rather than at a 2-5s Riftwalk.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json — Q range 650 cd 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, E cd 21/20/19/18/17, R cd 5/3.5/2 with 'Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana'; champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: Devour is promised from level 2: early "By level 2 you have the threat of the stun and Devour combination", spikes[1] (stage Lvl 3) "one slow into a stun into Devour", whys[1] "risks a stun-Devour that removes him from the wave", whys[2] at level 3.
audit.why: Devour is the ultimate and is not available before 6. Against Kassadin this matters more than usual because the whole strategic premise of the lane — kill him before he scales — depends on the player understanding exactly how much threat he has in the window where Kassadin is weakest. The real level-2-to-5 threat is a stun plus autos, which is still enough to bully a champion with a 650-range Q, but it is not a removal.
audit.corrected: Pre-6 the payoff is the Tongue Lash stun; Devour joins at 6.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour is the ultimate slot

audit.whatIsWrong: Nether Blade is never mentioned anywhere in the entry.
audit.why: It is an auto-attack reset on a 7s cooldown that restores mana on hit. Both halves matter: the reset means Kassadin's burst opens on an attack wind-up rather than a visible ability cast, so the tell a Tahm Kench should react to is not the one the entry describes; and the mana restore is the reason a Kassadin who is being denied CS can still afford to keep trading.
audit.corrected: Name Nether Blade as the auto-reset and mana-sustain tool, 7s cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json — W Nether Blade: 'next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage and restores Mana', cooldown 7, flag autoReset; _missing-interactions.json rule autoreset-burst-tell for tahmkench vs kassadin

audit.whatIsWrong: mid ends with "use Abyssal Voyage to roam and deny him the farm and XP safety he needs to get online".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not on the live champion. Tahm Kench has no global roam tool. The advice is also strategically inverted for this specific matchup: leaving the lane is how a scaling Kassadin gets the free farm the sentence is trying to deny him.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour. Denying Kassadin farm is done by holding the lane, not by roaming out of it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour, no global ability in kit

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 tops in the game — his only tool is Null Sphere's slow-projectile silence, and at level 1 he has no way to escape your Tongue Lash range. Step up, auto him, slow him with Q, and begin stacking An Acquired Taste immediately. He will try to Q you to stop an early all-in, so walk in with the Q slow already on him so the silence lands after your first stack, not before. By level 2 you have the threat of the stun and Devour combination, and he knows it — use that threat to bully him off every CS he walks up for.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest level-1 tops in the game — Null Sphere only reaches 650 against your 900, and at level 1 he has no way to escape Tongue Lash range. Step up, auto him, slow him with Q, and begin stacking An Acquired Taste immediately. His Q interrupts channels rather than silencing, so it cannot stop a Tongue Lash or a Devour cast at any point in the lane. By level 3 the stun is your threat — Devour is your ultimate and waits for 6 — and that stun alone bullies him off every CS he walks up for.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your lull window: Kassadin has no Riftwalk yet but he can play passive and poke with Null Sphere, which silences you briefly and stops a Devour cast if he times it at 2 stacks. Play the stack game patiently — slow with Q, get your auto, and only commit the stun when you have the third stack confirmed so a Null Sphere silence cannot interrupt the Devour. At level 6 the lane enters a genuine skill matchup: his Riftwalk lets him blink away from your Tongue Lash arc and blink back in on a short cooldown, resetting your stacks. Force him to Riftwalk in before you throw Q rather than after, and use Abyssal Voyage to roam and deny him the farm and XP safety he needs to get online.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your lull window: Kassadin has no Riftwalk yet and pokes with a 650-range Null Sphere that interrupts channels but cannot stop any cast of yours. Punish Force Pulse instead — at 21s on rank 1 it is far and away his longest cooldown, so the moment he spends the cone you have a real window to walk him down. At level 6 Riftwalk lets him blink out of Tongue Lash range on a 2-5s cooldown, but it does not touch your banked stacks, so hold them. What limits his chain-blinking is mana, not cooldown: force repeated Riftwalks and he prices himself out of the fight. His burst opens on a Nether Blade auto reset, so react to the attack wind-up, not to a visible cast.

edits.before: Kassadin's passive Force Pulse shield is magic-damage only and irrelevant at level 1 against your auto plus Tongue Lash slow — stack An Acquired Taste freely and set the tone of the lane.
edits.after: Void Stone gives him standing magic damage reduction, which will blunt Devour later, but at level 1 your auto plus Tongue Lash slow beats it outright — stack freely and set the tone.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks turn Devour into a silence-immune lockdown — his Null Sphere cannot interrupt it once stacks are confirmed, and he takes bonus damage while swallowed.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks make the Tongue Lash stun live; his Null Sphere interrupts channels only, so it never stops the cast, and Devour itself is still waiting on level 6.

edits.before: His Riftwalk comes online and he can now blink out of Tongue Lash's arc, genuinely resetting your stacks; the lane requires reads on his blink cooldown to punish, making it an even skirmish window.
edits.after: His Riftwalk comes online at a 2-5s cooldown, so he blinks out of Tongue Lash range at will — but your banked stacks survive it, and his escalating mana cost, not the cooldown, is the real limit.

edits.before: Tongue Lash's range lets you slow and stack An Acquired Taste on Kassadin before his passive shield regenerates, bullying him off CS he cannot afford to lose.
edits.after: Tongue Lash reaches 900 to Null Sphere's 650, so you slow and stack An Acquired Taste on Kassadin for free, bullying him off CS he cannot afford to lose.

edits.before: Three stacks online: one slow into a stun into Devour removes Kassadin from the wave entirely and he cannot Null Sphere or blink out of it.
edits.after: Three stacks online: the Tongue Lash stun lands and he has no blink until 6, so he eats it — Devour is your own ultimate and does not join until then.

edits.before: Kassadin's R comes online and he can now blink through your Tongue Lash arc and reset the stack count — respect his rift-walking and don't chase past your stun.
edits.after: Kassadin's R comes online at a 2-5s cooldown and he blinks out of Tongue Lash range — your stacks survive it, so hold them and don't chase past your stun.

edits.before: Keep him perpetually below 50% HP so his passive Force Pulse shield cannot absorb enough to make trades safe for him
edits.after: Trade before he lands Null Sphere, since the magic shield on it is what makes an exchange survivable for him

edits.before: Use Null Sphere's silence to interrupt your Devour cast once he sees you winding up at 2 stacks
edits.after: Open with a Nether Blade auto reset, then shield up with Null Sphere before the third stack

edits.before: Kite with Riftwalk blinks at level 6 to reset your An Acquired Taste stacks and avoid the stun-Devour window
edits.after: Kite with 2-5s Riftwalk blinks at 6 to stay outside Tongue Lash range until the banked stacks decay

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike at 6. Kill him before it scales. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Kassadin Force Pulse: the real window — 21s at rank 1, his longest cooldown. Riftwalk is 2-5s, so punish mana not timing. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Two flags on my own work here. First, the Null Sphere silence correction is Medium confidence, not High: I am reasoning from absence — Riot's text says 'interrupting channels' and the kit's flag vocabulary contains a 'silence' flag that Null Sphere does not carry — rather than from a positive statement that it does not silence. It is the strongest inference the local files support, and it matters enough to act on (four lines in this entry depend on it), but it is the one edit in my slice I would most want a human or a wiki check to confirm before it ships. Second, wants.foe[1]'s replacement says stacks 'decay', which the kit does not quantify; I used the word without a duration deliberately, since An Acquired Taste plainly is not permanent but no local source gives the number. If the applier wants zero unsourced implication there, cut the trailing clause. Beyond that: this matchup also carries the file-wide pre-6 Devour defect and the Abyssal Voyage substitution, both documented in my jayce and heimerdinger audits. The packet's 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' flag was correct — there was not a single number in the entry — and the edits above add the 900-vs-650 range gap, Force Pulse's 21s, Riftwalk's 2-5s and Null Sphere's real function.
